edges.description: Reduced TRNT1 activity limits addition of the CCA trinucleotide to tRNA 3' ends.
Mitochondrial tRNAs lacking the CCA end accumulate in patient cells.
Mature cytosolic tRNAs are depleted in patient cells.

Inferred. Defects in mitochondrial protein synthesis are an established cause of congenital sideroblastic anemia, and SIFD was placed in that group; a direct link from the TRNT1 mitochondrial tRNA defect to erythroid mitochondrial iron loading has not been measured.
Reduced tRNA maturation and abundance alter translation of distinct proteins and engage stress signalling.
The authors of the mechanistic study link disturbed protein homeostasis to the autoinflammatory phenotype; the signalling step between them is not defined.
The case authors propose that ER stress in immature bone marrow B cells underlies the peripheral B-cell deficiency.
The febrile episodes are aseptic and suppressed by TNF inhibition.
Neutrophilic dermatosis improved with etanercept in the reported case.
Arthritis is reported among the inflammatory features and resolved with etanercept in one case.
TNF inhibition reduced transfusion requirement, so inflammation contributes to the anemia in addition to the intrinsic erythroid defect.
Growth improved under TNF inhibition.
Gastrointestinal disturbance accompanies the aseptic febrile episodes.
Vomiting accompanies the cyclical aseptic febrile episodes.
Electrolyte disturbance occurs during the febrile episodes.
Ring-sideroblast erythropoiesis produces sideroblastic anemia.
The anemia is markedly microcytic.
In the most severe, antenatal presentation, erythropoiesis is extramedullary.

Inferred: in the reported kindred, fetal hydrops occurred alongside severe anemia and marked extramedullary erythropoiesis, consistent with anemia-driven hydrops; the paper does not test the mechanism.
Severe disease releases nucleated red cells into the circulation.
The maturation block leaves few peripheral B cells.
Without mature B cells, all immunoglobulin classes fall.
Inferred link from the organoid phenotype to photoreceptor degeneration.

nodes.description: TNF inhibitors (etanercept, adalimumab) suppress the autoinflammatory episodes and, in the original series, also reduced transfusion need and improved growth.
